name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 3 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{24}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{4\cdot 3+6\cdot (-5)+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{35}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{4\cdot 11+6\cdot 5+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot (-8)}{{11}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{210}{210}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ -17\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Since the set {a1,a2,a3} is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace S is given by

projSx=proja1x+proja2x+proja3x.

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of x onto Span{a1}, Span{a2}, and Span{a3}:

proja1x=x⋅a1a1⋅a1a1=4⋅1+6⋅1+3⋅0+(−17)⋅212+12+02+(−2)2a1=−246[1102]=[−4−40−8]proja2x=x⋅a2a2⋅a2a2=4⋅3+6⋅(−5)+3⋅0+(−17)⋅132+(−5)2+02+12a2=−3535[3−501]=[−350−1]proja3x=x⋅a3a3⋅a3a3=4⋅11+6⋅5+3⋅0+(−17)⋅(−8)112+52+02+(−8)2a2=210210[1150−8]=[1150−8]

Therefore, we have that

projSx=proja1x+proja2x+proja3x=[−4−40−8]+[−350−1]+[1150−8]=[460−17].
